blocks.h2: Why the Flange Matters in an Old Home
blocks.body: The flange is the ring that holds the toilet to the drain. In older Ravenswood homes, it's often cast iron or lead attached to the old pipe, and it can corrode or break. When that happens, the toilet rocks, the seal fails and water seeps into the floor, sometimes reaching the ceiling below. We repair or replace the flange before setting the toilet, so it stays tight.

blocks.h2: What Affects the Price of Toilet Work
blocks.body: Small repairs are quick. Replacing a corroded flange takes longer. Carrying a new toilet up narrow stairs adds a little time. We check and quote a flat price.

items.q: Why won't my toilet stay tight to the floor?
items.answer: Often a corroded cast iron flange. We repair or replace it and reset the toilet.

items.q: Why does my toilet keep running?
items.answer: Usually a worn flapper or fill valve.

items.q: My neighbor below has a stain. Is it my toilet?
items.answer: Possibly. A failed wax seal can leak through the floor. We check it first.

items.q: Can you install a toilet I bought?
items.answer: Yes, with a new seal and supply line.

items.q: Can a rocking toilet cause damage?
items.answer: Yes. It breaks the seal and lets water into the floor.

items.q: Can you replace a toilet in a small vintage bathroom?
items.answer: Yes. Compact models fit well in tight older bathrooms.

items.q: Why does my toilet clog in an older building?
items.answer: Older toilets clog more easily, and old drains can narrow with buildup. We'll check both.

items.q: How much does toilet repair cost in Ravenswood?
items.preview: It depends on the problem. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what's wrong and whether you're repairing or replacing. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
